prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability for the taking is undisputed; the trial will turn entirely on valuation. Given the frontage-heavy nature of the strips taken and typical Court of Claims outcomes for partial commercial takings without dramatic severance damage, an award meaningfully above the $302,460 advance payment but well short of the $2,000,000 demand is most likely, with the EDPL 304(H) clawback risk remaining low but not negligible.

issues.label: Just Compensation - Value of Taken Strips and Severance Damages

figures.label: Claimant's demand for just compensation

issues.label: Ground Lease / Leasehold Apportionment Effect on Owner's Recovery

outcome.description: After trial the Court of Claims found just compensation of $283,920 (adopting a before-taking value of $2,510,000 with a minor adjustment, $30,000 severance damages and $26,500 for three trees), below the $302,460 advance payment, and entered judgment for the State for the $18,540 difference under EDPL 304(H). The Second Department affirmed on July 14, 2021. Amount used is the compensation found for the taking (the owner's net recovery beyond the advance was negative).
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed; compensation of $283,920 was below the $302,460 advance, so the owner repays $18,540.
